record.context_brief: Rank of the average mixing matrix in primitive distance-regular graphs
record.original_question: Let G be a primitive distance-regular graph, and let Mc denote the average mixing matrix of its continuous-time quantum walk, defined by Mc = lim_{T -> infinity} (1/T) integral from 0 to T of M(t) dt, where M(t) = U(t) o U(-t) and U(t) = exp(itA). Prove that the rank of Mc is equal to the number of vertices of G.

evidence.quote: The average mixing matrix is defined as Mc = lim T→∞ Mc[0,T], and a straightforward calculation shows that if A(G) = Σ θrEr, then Mc = Σ Er ◦ Er.
4.1 Open Problem. If G is a primitive distance-regular graph, show that the rank of Mc is equal to the number of vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A$. The continuous-time quantum walk on $G$ is given by the family of unitary matrices $U(t) = \exp(itA)$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$. The mixing matrix at time $t$ is the doubly stochastic matrix
$$M(t) = U(t) \circ \overline{U(t)} = U(t) \circ U(-t),$$
where $\circ$ denotes the Schur (entrywise) product. The average mixing matrix is
$$M_c = \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T M(t)\, dt.$$
Equivalently, if $A = \sum_r \theta_r E_r$ is the spectral decomposition of $A$ into projections onto distinct eigenspaces, then
$$M_c = \sum_r E_r \circ E_r.$$

Recall that a connected graph $G$ of diameter $d$ is distance-regular if, for the distance-$i$ matrices $A_i$ ($0 \le i \le d$), there exist constants $p^k_{ij}$ such that $A_i A_j = \sum_k p^k_{ij} A_k$. A distance-regular graph is called primitive if each of its distance-$i$ graphs (for $1 \le i \le d$) is connected.

Prove that for every primitive distance-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, the rank of the average mixing matrix $M_c$ equals $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about the rank of the average mixing matrix for primitive distance-regular graphs. Web search returned general references on average mixing matrices and distance-regular graphs but no resolution of this specific conjecture; it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A New Perspective on the Average Mixing Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the average mixing matrix of continuous-time quantum walks and its rank-related properties.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on rank of average mixing matrix exists but does not settle the primitive distance-regular case.

status_evidence.title: A Quantum Walk Mixing Average Mixing Matrices (Godsil)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses average mixing matrices arising from continuous quantum walks on graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Background reference; no proof of the conjectured rank equality for primitive distance-regular graphs.
